name: Creamy Shrimp Pasta with Corn and Tomatoes
why: Peak summer corn and cherry tomatoes are at their sweetest right now, and this 30-minute pasta puts them front and center in a silky cream sauce with garlicky shrimp. Fresh, fast, and exactly what you want when it's hot outside.
author: Henry
ingredients: 8 oz linguine, spaghetti, or similar pasta
2-3 ears fresh sweet corn, kernels cut off the cob (cooked or grilled)
Salt and freshly cracked black pepper to taste

steps: Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a boil.
Mince the garlic cloves. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Cut kernels off the corn cobs.
Chop the spinach and tear the basil leaves. Set aside.
Cook pasta in boiling water according to package directions until al dente.
Before draining, reserve about 1/2 cup of the starchy pasta water.
Drain pasta, toss with a drizzle of olive oil to prevent sticking, and set aside.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Add 1 tablespoon butter to the pan. Add shrimp and sprinkle with 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Cook shrimp for 1-2 minutes per side until pink and opaque throughout.
Remove shrimp from the pan and set aside, covering loosely to keep warm.
In the same skillet, add the minced garlic and remaining 1 tablespoon butter. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the halved cherry tomatoes and corn kernels. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until tomatoes just begin to soften.
Add the chopped spinach and sauté until just wilted, about 30 seconds.
Return the cooked shrimp to the pan. Add remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Pour in the heavy cream and bring to a gentle simmer — do not boil vigorously.
Toss the cooked pasta directly into the skillet with the sauce, coating every strand.
Add reserved pasta water a splash at a time if the sauce seems too thick — it should coat the back of a spoon.
Season with freshly cracked black pepper and more salt to taste.
Plate immediately. Top generously with torn fresh basil and grated Parmesan.
Serve right away while the shrimp is still warm and the sauce is silky.

pro_tips: Grill the corn on the cob before cutting off the kernels — the smoky char adds a layer of flavor that boiled corn can't match.
Don't overcook the shrimp. They go from perfect to rubbery in seconds. Remove them as soon as they turn opaque and pink.
